about.title: Turlock Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: A shift in Turlock can end in a hospital bed for a lot of reasons: a forklift that rolls the wrong way, a slick floor nobody flagged, a ladder that gives out, or a delivery run that turns into a collision on Geer Road or N Golden State Boulevard. Stanislaus County saw 331 injury collisions inside Turlock city limits in 2025, with 473 people hurt, and some of those drivers were simply doing their jobs. When you are injured at work in California, workers' compensation is usually your only claim against your employer, and fault does not matter. What many Turlock workers do not realize is that a separate claim may exist against a third party, such as a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of faulty equipment, or another motorist on W Main Street. That second path has its own two-year deadline and can cover losses workers' comp leaves out. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Turlock Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Two Claims, Not One
items.desc: Workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party can be held responsible separately. An attorney can look at both so nothing gets left on the table.

items.title: Deadlines That Do Not Wait
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party claim carries a two-year statute of limitations. Getting connected early keeps both windows open.

items.title: Protection From Pushback
items.desc: Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal in California. The attorney you are matched with can help you stand on that right without fear of losing your job.

items.question: I was hit by another driver while making a work delivery in Turlock. Is that workers' comp or a car accident claim?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of who caused the crash. Since the other driver is a third party, you may also bring a separate injury claim against them, which can address pain, suffering, and other losses workers' comp does not pay. An attorney can coordinate the two so they do not work against each other.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' compensation claim. If you experience demotion, reduced hours, or termination after reporting, tell the attorney you are connected with right away.

items.question: How does LawProactive work, and what does it cost?
items.answer: LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. You share the basics of what happened, and we connect you with an independent personal injury attorney in our network. Those attorneys work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
